newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nobel prize winner hopes for pressure on Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Nobel prize winner hopes for pressure on Indonesia.

text.p: East Timor's Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, in an interview published on Sunday, said he was not surprised that the Indonesian government could not understand why he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
"They will never understand," Belo told the German news magazine Focus. "I hope the (Indonesian) government will now finally wake up."

Belo won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize jointly with East Timor independence activist Jose Ramos-Horta for their efforts to bring peace in the territory which Indonesia invaded after Portuguese colonisers left in 1975.

Indonesia reacted angrily to the award with Foreign Ministry spokesman Ghaffar Fadyl calling Ramos-Horta, 48, a "political opportunist". He avoided comment on Belo, 50, East Timor's outspoken Roman Catholic bishop.
Belo told the Munich-based Focus that he was hopeful the award would draw the world's attention to East Timor.

"The world will now take the problems of East Timor seriously again," Belo said. "I hope the Indonesian government will learn something. But we are still far away from our goal of equality and more rights for the people of East Timor."
